structure: Part 3, Dashboard and notification actions, read in full at frontend HEAD 4c2119da: the dashboard feature (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, notification-helper.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, view-model/sort-options.js, view-model/row/index.js, view-model/row/actions.js, dashboard.fit.spec.js), notification-actions (controller.js, notification-actions.fit.spec.js), cancel-amend (controller.js, template.njk, copy en/cy, cancel-amend.fit.spec.js) and delete-notification (controller.js, template.njk, copy en/cy, delete-notification.fit.spec.js), all under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/. To read what those files render, it also looked up, without claiming their wider content: shared/paths.js (route shapes), shared/kit.js (status tag text and colours, CYA slug), shared/copy.en.js (notification action, recoverable error and stale action copy), shared/layout.njk banners, config/nunjucks/context/context.js (staleAction query flag), flow/section-captions (the Dashboard caption), sets/live-animals/set.js (the /live-animals base) and engine/journey.js (which notifications are listed and what amend, copy, cancel-amend and delete do). Pages covered: the dashboard at GET / (heading, start button, filter panel with reference search, sort, results label, notification cards with eight fields, status tags, row actions per status, pagination, empty states, success banners), the create POST /notifications and amend POST /notifications/{id}/amend routes, the copy POST /notifications/{id}/copy action, the cancel-amend page GET/POST /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend and the delete page GET/POST /notifications/{id}/delete. Every test in the four fit specs gets a claim: dashboard 15 tests in 6 describes, notification-actions 4, cancel-amend 5, delete-notification 5. The unit tests (controller.test.js, copy.test.js, index.test.js, notification-helper.test.js) sit in the folders but are not in this part's read list and were not claimed. Claims run dashboard, row actions, create and amend, copy, cancel-amend, delete, then each fit spec's tests, then gaps.

claims.statement: The dashboard is the GET route at the root of the live-animals set, so a user reaches it at /live-animals.
claims.note: SET_ID = 'live-animals' and SET_BASE = `/${SET_ID}`; dashboardPath() returns the set base.

claims.statement: The dashboard shows the section caption 'Dashboard' above its heading, in the extra-large caption style.
The dashboard's page title and extra-large heading are 'Import notification service'.
Under the heading, the dashboard explains the service in one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals.
claims.quote: 'Use this service to tell the authorities about live animals ' + 'you are importing. You will answer a short set of questions ' + 'about the consignment, then submit your notification.'

claims.statement: The dashboard has a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' in a form that posts to /live-animals/notifications.
Posting to /notifications creates a new notification, adds it to the notifications the user's session knows, and begins an opening run for it.
claims.quote:
const journey = await startJourney(request, h)
  await beginOpeningRun(request, h, journey.journeyId)

claims.statement: After creating a notification, the user is sent straight to that notification's origin page, not to the overview.
Below the start button, the dashboard has a medium heading 'Your notifications'.
The notification list is laid out in two columns: a filter panel in the left one-third and the results, sort and cards in the right two-thirds.
The filter panel is headed 'Filter notifications'.
The filter panel has one text field, labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label), named referenceNumber, with no hint.
The filter panel's 'Search' button submits a GET to the dashboard with the reference as the referenceNumber query parameter.
A search keeps the sort order the user has chosen, carried as a hidden field in the search form.
claims.quote:
{% if sort %}
            <input type="hidden" name="sort" value="{{ sort }}" />

claims.statement: A search does not keep the page number: the search form carries no page field, so a search starts at page 1.
claims.note: Read from the absence of a page hidden input in the search form, against the sort form which does carry one.

claims.statement: The search term is trimmed, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter.
claims.quote:
const trimmed = value.trim()
  return trimmed.length > 0 ? trimmed : undefined

claims.statement: The search field is filled with the term currently searched for, so the term stays visible after the search.
Although the label says 'Keyword or reference', the term is passed to the notification listing only as a reference number; nothing in this slice searches by any other keyword.
claims.note: Whether the backend matches exactly or partially is outside this slice; the fit spec proves an exact reference match only. The label and the behaviour may disagree.

claims.statement: The reference search is the only filter on the dashboard: there is no filter by status, date, commodity or party.
claims.note: Read from the filter panel holding a single input.

claims.statement: Above the cards, a small bold results label says how many notifications are shown: 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' (one item on a page) or 'Showing S to E of T Results'.
claims.quote:
none: 'No Results',
      one: 'Showing 1 Result',
      oneOf: (item, total) => `Showing ${item} of ${total} Results`,
      many: (start, end, total) =>
        `Showing ${start} to ${end} of ${total} Results`
claims.note: The helper's own fallbacks differ ('Showing 1 Results'), but the controller always passes the copy labels. 'Results' is capitalised mid-sentence in the copy.

claims.statement: The results range is worked out from the page number, the page size the listing returns and the number of rows shown: start is (page-1) times size plus 1, end is capped at the total.
When a reference search finds nothing, the results label reads 'No notifications found' instead of 'No Results'.
When the user has no notifications and is not searching, the dashboard says 'You have not started any notifications in this session.'
claims.quote: emptyText: 'You have not started any notifications in this session.'

claims.statement: When a reference search finds nothing, the empty-state sentence is not shown; only the results label says nothing was found.
The dashboard lists only notifications the user's session knows: the listing is asked for the journey ids held in the session, not for every notification the user or their organisation owns.
claims.quote:
const journeyIds = await session.knownJourneyIds(request)
  return records.list({ journeyIds, page, sort, referenceNumber })
claims.note: The empty-state copy ('in this session') matches this. A notification opened directly by id is added to the known set (engine/journey.js:110-112).

claims.statement: Deleted notifications are left out of the dashboard list.
claims.note: The filter runs after the listing is paged, so a page holding a deleted row could show fewer rows than the page size while the totals still count it.

claims.statement: The sort control is a select labelled 'Sort by' (small bold label).

The sort options are, in order: 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)', 'Date created (oldest to newest)', with values arrivalDate,desc, arrivalDate,asc, createdAt,desc and createdAt,asc.
claims.quote:
{ value: 'arrivalDate,desc', text: 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' },
  { value: 'arrivalDate,asc', text: 'Arrival (oldest to newest)' },
  { value: 'createdAt,desc', text: 'Date created (newest to oldest)' },
  { value: 'createdAt,asc', text: 'Date created (oldest to newest)' }

claims.statement: The default sort is arrival date, newest first; any sort value not in the list falls back to it.
The sort is applied with a secondary 'Update sort' button; the dashboard does not re-sort when the select changes.
Changing the sort keeps the current page (when beyond page 1) and the current reference search.
Dashboard links write page only when beyond 1, sort only when not the default, and referenceNumber only when searching.
A page number that is not a whole number or is below 1 is treated as page 1, and one beyond the last page is treated as the last page.
Pagination shows 'Previous' and 'Next' links only when there is more than one page: no Previous on the first page and no Next on the last.
Previous and Next links keep the current sort and reference search.
Pagination is previous and next only: there are no numbered page links.
claims.note: Read from buildPaginationLinks returning only previous and next, with no items array for govukPagination.

claims.statement: The page size comes from the notification listing, not the frontend; the fit spec proves 20 notifications a page.
claims.note: The controller reads size from listed.size; the 20 is set by the backend and proven by the fit spec.

claims.statement: Each notification is shown as a summary card titled with its reference, falling back to its journey id when it has no reference.
Each card shows eight fields in three rows: Commodity, Origin and 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor and Status; 'Date created' and 'Date submitted'.
claims.quote:
status: 'Status',
    commodity: 'Commodity',
    origin: 'Origin',
    arrival: 'Arrival at destination',
    consignor: 'Consignor',
    consignee: 'Consignee',
    created: 'Date created',
    submitted: 'Date submitted',
claims.note: Consignee is shown before Consignor on the card, though the copy lists consignor first.

claims.statement: The card's Commodity shows the commodity's name for its code, falling back through name, display name, text, commodity code, code and value; blank when there is no commodity.
The card's Origin shows the display label of the country of origin, and is blank when no country is chosen.
The card's 'Arrival at destination' shows the arrival date the user chose, as that calendar day regardless of the server's time zone.
claims.quote:
// arrival is a day the user chose; created and submitted are moments.
  arrival: formatDisplayCalendarDate(journey.arrivalDate),

claims.statement: The card's 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' show the day the event happened in the service's time zone, not the server's.
claims.quote:
A moment that happened — created, submitted. Rendered as the day it
 * happened in the service's zone, not the container's ambient `TZ`

claims.statement: A missing or unparseable date shows as blank on the card, so a notification not yet submitted shows an empty 'Date submitted'.
The dashboard copy holds 'Not submitted', but the card never renders it: an unsubmitted notification shows a blank 'Date submitted'.
claims.note: Read from the key being absent from the template and the row view model. Likewise the 'Reference' and 'Actions' table headings in copy (copy.en.js:16,25) are not rendered.

claims.statement: The card's Consignor and Consignee show the party names, blank when none is chosen.
The card's Status is a tag: 'Draft' in blue, 'Submitted' in green, 'Amending' in yellow and 'Deleted' in grey.
claims.note: Classes govuk-tag--blue, --green, --yellow, --grey. Deleted rows are filtered from the dashboard, so the grey tag does not appear there.

claims.statement: A submitted notification's card offers four actions, in order: View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete.
View is a link to the notification's read-only view at /notifications/{id}/notification-view.
Amend is a button that posts to /notifications/{id}/amend.
A draft notification's card offers three actions, in order: Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete.
Resume is a link to the notification's overview (hub) at /notifications/{id}.
A notification being amended offers four actions, in order: Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete.
'Cancel amendment' is a link to the cancel-amend page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend.
A notification in any other status has no actions on its card.
The action labels are 'View', 'Amend', 'Resume', 'Cancel amendment', 'Copy as new' and 'Delete'.
claims.note: 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' come from shared copy notificationActions.

claims.statement: Every card action carries visually hidden text 'notification {reference}', so a screen reader hears, for example, 'Delete notification GBN-AG-…'.
Card actions that change data (Amend, 'Copy as new') are forms posting with the CSRF crumb, rendered as link-styled buttons; the others are plain links.
'Copy as new' sends the notification's concurrency token and the origin 'dashboard' with the copy request.
Delete on a card is a link to the delete confirmation page at /notifications/{id}/delete, not an immediate delete.
Amend works only on a notification the session knows; anything else sends the user back to the dashboard.

Amending a submitted notification puts it into amendment and opens its overview; amending a draft or one already being amended opens its overview without changing it; any other status returns to the dashboard.
claims.note: The engine is outside this part's read list; read only to say where the amend route leads.

claims.statement: With ?deleted=1, the dashboard shows a green success banner titled 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.'
claims.quote:
successTitle: 'Notification deleted',
      successBody: 'The notification has been deleted.'

claims.statement: With ?copied=1, the dashboard shows a success banner titled 'Notification copied' with 'A new draft notification has been created.'
claims.quote:
successTitle: 'Notification copied',
      successBody: 'A new draft notification has been created.'

claims.statement: Nothing in this slice sends the user to the dashboard with ?copied=1: a successful copy goes to the new draft's overview, so the 'Notification copied' banner is never reached from 'Copy as new'.
claims.note: Whether the hub shows its own copy banner belongs to part 4.

claims.statement: Both dashboard success banners are announced to assistive technology as alerts.

When a copy from the dashboard fails to save, the dashboard is shown again with HTTP 500 and the 'There is a problem' banner saying 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
claims.quote: body: 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
claims.note: The shared body talks about answers on this page being saved, which does not fit a failed copy from the dashboard.

claims.statement: With ?staleAction=1, the dashboard shows the banner 'The notification has been updated' with 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.'
claims.quote:
title: 'The notification has been updated',
    body: 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.'

claims.statement: The dashboard's Welsh copy is a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator, and must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.quote: // MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

claims.statement: In Welsh the dashboard is titled 'Gwasanaeth hysbysu mewnforio', its start button reads 'Dechrau hysbysiad newydd' and its list heading 'Eich hysbysiadau'.
claims.note: Every English dashboard key has a Welsh twin in copy.cy.js, including sort options, results labels, action labels and the empty state.

claims.statement: The Welsh sort option labels are hard-wired in order to the four sort values; the English labels in the helper are replaced by the localised copy.
'Copy as new' is the POST route /notifications/{id}/copy.
Copy creates a new, separate notification from the source, adds it to the session's known notifications, and sends the user to the new notification's overview.
claims.quote:
const copied = await records.copy(journeyId, concurrencyToken, actor)
  await session.addKnownJourney(request, h, copied.journeyId)

claims.statement: Copy works only on a notification the session knows; anything else sends the user back to the dashboard with no banner.

Copy checks the concurrency token the page held; if the notification has changed since, the user is sent back where they started with ?staleAction=1 and sees the 'The notification has been updated' banner.
Copy can start from the dashboard or from the notification view; the copyOrigin field decides where a stale or failed copy returns the user.
claims.note: For a stale copy from the notification view the redirect uses the slug 'check-answers', while the view itself lives at 'notification-view' (kit.CYA_SLUG). Whether a check-answers route exists is outside this slice; the two may not match.

claims.statement: When a copy fails to save, the page the copy came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner.
Copying a notification that holds address-book parties raises a NotificationCreated event that resolves those parties, so the acting user's organisation id travels with the copy call.
The cancel-amend page is GET and POST at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend.
The cancel-amend page shows only for a notification being amended; for a submitted one it redirects to the notification view, and for any other status to the dashboard.
The cancel-amend page's title and large heading are 'Cancel this amendment?', with no section caption.
The cancel-amend page warns that changes made since amending began will be discarded and the submitted version restored.
claims.quote: body: 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.'

claims.statement: The cancel-amend page's primary button is 'Yes, cancel amendment', a standard (not warning) button that posts the form.
The cancel-amend page's secondary button 'No, return to notification' links to the notification view and leaves the amendment in place.
The cancel-amend page's back link goes to the notification view.
The cancel-amend form posts the CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token.
Confirming cancel-amend restores the submitted version and sends the user to the notification view with ?cancelled=1; if the session does not know the notification, it returns to the dashboard.
Posting cancel-amend for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and redirects as the GET does.
When cancelling an amendment fails to save, the cancel-amend page is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner.
The cancel-amend page has Welsh copy, a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator: 'Canslo’r diwygiad hwn?', 'Iawn, canslo’r diwygiad' and 'Na, dychwelyd i’r hysbysiad'.
The delete page is GET and POST at /notifications/{id}/delete.
A draft, submitted or amending notification can be deleted; for any other status the delete page redirects to the dashboard.
claims.quote:
journey.status === state.DRAFT ||
  journey.status === state.SUBMITTED ||
  journey.status === state.AMEND

claims.statement: The delete page's title and large heading are 'Delete this notification?', with no section caption.
The delete page warns 'This cannot be undone.'
The delete page does not name the notification it will delete: no reference appears on the page.
claims.note: The layout may show a journey strip with the reference (kit.base passes journey); that strip is outside this slice. The cancel-amend page is the same.

claims.statement: The delete page's primary button is the red warning button 'Yes, delete notification'.
The delete page's secondary button 'No, return to dashboard' links to the dashboard.
The delete page's back link goes to the dashboard.
The delete form posts the CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token.
Confirming delete soft-deletes the notification (it is marked deleted, not removed) and sends the user to the dashboard with ?deleted=1.
Deleting a notification the session does not know changes nothing and returns to the dashboard with no banner.
Posting delete for a notification not in a deletable status changes nothing and returns to the dashboard.
When a delete fails to save, the delete page is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner.

Deleting a submitted notification that holds address-book parties raises a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event that resolves those parties, so the backend needs the acting user's organisation id and the frontend forwards it.
The delete page has Welsh copy, a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator: "Dileu'r hysbysiad hwn?", 'Ni ellir dadwneud hyn.', "Iawn, dileu'r hysbysiad" and "Na, dychwelyd i'r dangosfwrdd".
claims.note: The Welsh delete copy uses a straight apostrophe where the cancel-amend Welsh copy uses a curly one.

claims.statement: No fit spec in this slice proves deleting or cancel-amending a notification while amending, or the redirects for a non-deletable or non-amending notification.
No fit spec in this slice proves the dashboard's 'Notification copied' banner, the recoverable-error banner after a failed action, or the Welsh dashboard.

The slice does not say whether a user can see notifications started in an earlier session or by colleagues in their organisation; the dashboard lists only the session's known notifications, and nothing records whether that is intended.
